newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: CRICKET-SECURITY TIGHT AFTER BANGLADESH WIN ICC TROPHY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SECURITY TIGHT AFTER BANGLADESH WIN ICC TROPHY.

text.p: Hundreds of riot police and securitymen took up positions in Dhaka on Sunday after Bangladesh won the International Cricket Council (ICC) trophy in Kuala Lumpur, witnesses said.
Police said they were taking strict security measures to prevent any outbreak of violence by cricket fans.
Thousands of people poured into the streets and bands played to celebrate the win against Kenya in the final.
Bangladesh beat Kenya to win the International Cricket Council (ICC) trophy in the Malaysian capital.
Bangladesh, set a revised target of 166 in 25 overs in the match, scored the winning run off the last ball. Kenya scored 241 for seven in stipulated 50 overs on Saturday.

Bangladesh has banned the spraying of coloured water and explosion of crackers after at least two people were killed and 100 injured during an euphoric celebration of Bangladesh's semi-final win over Scotland on Wednesday. The win has assured Bangladesh's place in the 1999 World Cup in England.
Witnesses said people took to the streets of Dhaka immediately after the result of the game. They were carrying Bangladesh flags and showering flower petals on cars and passers-by.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sent a message congratulating the players in Kuala Lumpur on their victory, Bangladesh's greatest success as a cricket-playing nation.
Hasina has already pledged a car for all players if Bangladesh qualified for the World Cup.
